observation_summary: The methods iterateDomainBounds and iterateRangeBounds in DatasetUtilities were failing to correctly calculate the bounds of datasets because they ignored the primary value (x or y) and only considered the start and end interval values, leading to incorrect range calculations and potential NullPointerExceptions when bounds were not properly initialized or updated.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves modifying the core logic of how bounds are calculated by including the primary value (x or y) in the min/max calculations, in addition to the start and end interval values. This is a correction to the algorithm used to determine the dataset bounds. It is not a simple missing check (Checking) or a simple assignment error (Assignment/Initialization), but a fundamental change in the procedure used to compute the range.
evidence_used: The fix adds logic to retrieve and include the primary value (x or y) in the min/max calculations for both domain and range bounds.
The fix updates the min/max logic to correctly account for all three components (value, start value, end value) of the interval data.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks for Double.isNaN, the primary purpose of the change is to include the missing 'value' component in the calculation, which is an algorithmic correction.
The fix is not about initializing a variable, but about changing the logic of the calculation loop.
